title: bonsai.ask/1
description: The ask record (contract §9.1): an agent (or the ladder) asks a person something typed, and a person answers. One JSON line, at most 8,192 bytes, appended to the main checkout's .bonsai/local/asks/<YYYY-MM-DD>.ndjson (one file per UTC day), never committed. Written by bonsai ask, bonsai answer and Bonsai's ladder runner (Bless); read by bonsai asks, agents (bonsai ask --status) and the studio's bridge. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null or [] where it does not apply (contract §2.2, §2.5); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one, and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version, always the first field (contract §2.2). Today's record wrote v: 1.

id.description: A UUID for the record; a replay with the same id is a duplicate.

at.description: When it was written: ISO-8601 UTC (with milliseconds, as today).

op.description: What the record does, a closed list (contract §2.2, §9.1): file (asks), resolve (withdraws), answer (a person's answer).

key.description: <source>:<part>: the agent's --key, or h- and 12 hex characters hashed from type, target and title; Bless's is ladder:bless-<task>. The key names no project: the bridge adds its own when forwarding (contract §9.1).

workspace.description: The workspace id from bonsai.yaml (contract §3). Today's field: project.

source.description: Who filed it: agent or ladder (contract §9.1, as today). Only the ladder files Bless.

session.description: The asking session's id, or null.

type.description: The ask's type: Answer, Decide, Look or Play from agents, Bless from the ladder, or a type a pack defines (an open list). null where it does not apply (today: on a resolve).

task.description: The task id the ask is about (never a path), or null.

doc.description: The document id the ask is about (never a path), or null.

title.description: As today: the question, one line, redacted, at most 300 characters; null where it does not apply (today: on a resolve).
examples: Which colour should the dark theme use for links?

why.description: As today: why it is asked, redacted, at most 600 characters; null where it does not apply (today: on a resolve).
examples: The design file gives two blues and the contrast check passes for both.

then_text.description: As today: what happens after the answer, redacted, at most 300 characters; null when not given.
examples: The builder applies the chosen colour and reruns the contrast check.

options.description: As today: a Decide's choices, at most four, each one line of at most 200 characters, each different; [] for every other type and where it does not apply (today: on a resolve).

verdict.description: As today: on a Look, the agent's own verdict, pass or fail; null otherwise.

data.description: A pack type's payload, or null. Bless's (today's bless field): {task, head, result_sha, rises: [{name, was, now, new_tests}]} (contract §9.1, §11). Typed open: the payload is the type's own.

answer.description: For op answer: who answered, how, and what; null on every other op (contract §9.1).

examples.words: Darker reads better on the old monitors.

by.description: terminal, or the caller's own reference, as text of at most 60 characters. Bonsai stores what it is given; its code names no caller.

via.description: Free text naming who carried the answer, at most 30 characters, or null.

choice.description: The option chosen, for a Decide; null otherwise.

verdict.description: The person's verdict, pass or fail, for a Look; null otherwise.

words.description: The person's own words, redacted (at most 2,000 characters, as today), or null.
examples: Darker reads better on the old monitors.
